module purpose: neorv32_cpu_alu reads operands rs1_i, rs2_i, rs3_i and the control record ctrl_i; it compares rs1_i with rs2_i (cmp_o), selects operands and adds or subtracts them (add_o), drives the result of the operation chosen by ctrl_i.alu_op on res_o, hands operands to co-processor sub-units whose results and valid flags it merges (res_o, done_o), tracks a CFU operation in cfu_busy, and routes co-processor CSR write enables and CSR read data (csr_o).

use-case flows.value: comparison of rs1_i with rs2_i (equal, less-than, signed or unsigned) exported on cmp_o and wired to the bitmanip and FPU sub-units
operand selection (rs1_i or ctrl_i.pc_cur, rs2_i or ctrl_i.alu_imm) and the add/subtract result exported on add_o
result of the operation selected by ctrl_i.alu_op (zero, add, co-processor, set-less-than, move, xor, or, and) driven on res_o
co-processor dispatch: operands, shift amount and control wired to the sub-units; their results collected in cp_result and OR-merged into cp_res
CFU operation request (ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu) that starts the CFU and sets cfu_busy
co-processor completion: sub-unit valid flags, the qualified CFU valid, merged into done_o
CSR write to an FPU or CFU CSR: address match, write enable, CSR address and write data passed to the sub-unit
FPU or CFU CSR read data selected by the address match and returned on csr_o
cfu_busy and cp_result(4) cleared while rstn_i is '0'; cfu_busy cleared on CFU done or trap; cp_result(4) zeroed when no accepted CFU result

conceptual assets.concept: Operand comparison result -- whether rs1_i equals rs2_i and whether rs1_i is less than rs2_i, signed or unsigned
conceptual assets.reasoning: The comparison flow computes `cmp(cmp_equal_c) <= '1' when (rs1_i = rs2_i) else '0';` (line 100) and `cmp(cmp_less_c) <= '1' when (signed(cmp_rs1) < signed(cmp_rs2)) else '0';` (line 101); ctrl_i.alu_unsigned decides the sign extension of the compared operands (lines 97-98). The decision leaves through `cmp_o <= cmp;` (line 102) and is wired into the cmp_i inputs of the bitmanip and FPU sub-units (lines 230, 263), whose users are not supplied, so Integrity is Established as these consumers receiving exactly the result of the predicates at lines 100-101. cmp computes (CONSTRAINED_BY rs1_i, rs2_i, occurrence 2); cmp_o is the exit port (COPIES cmp, occurrence 2); rs1_i and rs2_i set it (CONSTRAINS cmp, occurrence 5, line 100); ctrl_i sets it through its field alu_unsigned (SOURCES cmp_rs1, occurrence 2, line 97). cmp_rs1 and cmp_rs2 are sign-extended operands of the condition, not its result. The flow graph lists cmp and cmp_o as not reached from an input because CONSTRAINS is a control edge; the RTL shows the dependency at lines 100-101. Confidentiality is not established: no line restricts who observes cmp_o.

conceptual assets.reasoning: Each sub-unit drives its slot of cp_result (lines 176, 199, 235, 268, 372, 406); the CFU result is accepted into cp_result(4) only when `if (cfu_done = '1') and ((ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu = '1') or (cfu_busy = '1')) then` (lines 334-335) and is zeroed otherwise (line 337). conceptual assets.concept: Co-processor completion event -- the signal that a co-processor operation has finished
conceptual assets.reasoning: `done_o <= cp_valid(0) or cp_valid(1) or cp_valid(2) or cp_valid(3) or cp_valid(4) or cp_valid(5) or cp_valid(6);` (line 147) reports completion from the sub-units' valid_o outputs (lines 177, 200, 236, 269, 373, 407) and, for the CFU, from `cp_valid(4) <= cfu_done and (ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu or cfu_busy);` (line 343), which qualifies the CFU's valid_o (line 314) by an active request. The consumer of done_o is not supplied, so Integrity is Established as done_o asserting exactly when a valid flag defined by these lines is set. Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: when a sub-unit asserts valid_o, done_o asserts in the same cycle (line 147). done_o is the exit port (GATED_BY cp_valid, occurrence 2); cp_valid computes (CONNECTS from neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter_inst.valid_o, occurrence 9; its CFU bit is GATED_BY cfu_done at line 343); cfu_done computes (CONNECTS from neorv32_cpu_cp_cfu_inst.valid_o, occurrence 2), and this entity tests it in if conditions to clear cfu_busy and accept the CFU result (lines 329, 334). cfu_done exists only when RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu (line 291).

conceptual assets.concept: CFU operation-in-progress state -- whether a custom-function-unit operation has been started and not yet finished or aborted
conceptual assets.reasoning: `elsif (ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu = '1') then` / `cfu_busy <= '1';` (lines 331-332) sets the state, `if (cfu_done = '1') or (ctrl_i.cpu_trap = '1') then` / `cfu_busy <= '0';` (lines 329-330) clears it, and the reset arm clears it (line 326). The state decides whether a CFU result is accepted into cp_result(4) (line 334), whether cp_valid(4) asserts (line 343), and the CFU's active_i through `cfu_active <= ctrl_i.alu_cp_cfu or cfu_busy;` (lines 342, 299). Integrity is Established: a wrong state accepts a CFU result that was not requested or drops a requested one (lines 334-337), and the CFU receives a wrong active_i. Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: the state is released when the CFU reports done or a trap occurs (line 329). cfu_busy stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4) and its own records show its use (GATES cp_result, line 334; GATES cfu_active, line 342); cfu_active computes the active decision delivered to the CFU sub-unit (GATED_BY cfu_busy, occurrence 3); ctrl_i sets the state through alu_cp_cfu (GATES cfu_busy, occurrence 30, line 331) and cpu_trap (line 329). All exist only when RISCV_ISA_Zxcfu (line 291); otherwise cfu_busy and cfu_active are tied to '0' (lines 351-352).

conceptual assets.reasoning: `fpu_csr_en <= '1' when (ctrl_i.csr_addr(11 downto 2) = csr_fflags_c(11 downto 2)) else '0';` (line 273) and `fpu_csr_we <= fpu_csr_en and ctrl_i.csr_we;` (line 274) decide the FPU CSR write, wired to csr_we_i (line 258) together with ctrl_i.csr_addr(1 downto 0) and ctrl_i.csr_wdata (lines 259-260); lines 318-319 and 301-303 do the same for the CFU. The CSRs are inside sub-units that are not supplied, so Integrity is Established as each sub-unit receiving exactly the write enable these predicates define (lines 273-274, 318-319). fpu_csr_we and cfu_csr_we compute the decision (GATED_BY ctrl_i.csr_we, occurrence 3); ctrl_i sets it through csr_we (GATES fpu_csr_we, occurrence 20, line 274), and its fields csr_addr and csr_wdata are wired into the sub-units. fpu_csr_en and cfu_csr_en also qualify the read data (GATES csr_rdata_fpu, line 275; GATES csr_rdata_cfu, line 320), so they are operands of the write decision, not the decision.
